pages.title: Why are there two glasses at my place setting?
pages.snippet: Water glass, wine glass, mystery glass: a short guide to finding your drink.
blocks: A guest writes: “There are two glasses beside my plate. Have I accidentally booked dinner for two?”
Not necessarily. A single place setting may include a water glass and a wine glass. At receptions, staff may also prepare glassware before guests arrive.
Count place settings, not just glasses: plates, cutlery and chairs provide the context. A photograph of a table does not tell you which glasses were used.
If neither glass contains your drink, try asking the waiter. Staring meaningfully at the table remains an experimental technique.

pages.title: Two glasses, one gift box | The Toast Rack
pages.snippet: A boxed pair of wine glasses. For anniversaries, housewarmings and ambitious solo evenings.
blocks: Two matching wine glasses in a presentation box. Clear glass, slender stems, absolutely no ability to improve the wine.
Popular for wedding gifts, housewarmings and replacing the two glasses you broke while explaining how careful you are.
Gift message optional. “You already own these” is not currently available as a printed greeting.
Price: £18 per pair. Wine not included. A surprisingly common source of disappointment.

pages.title: Two glasses at once? | The Spare Pair Forum
pages.snippet: One pair on your nose. One on your head. Still looking for your glasses.
blocks: THREAD: Does anyone else keep two glasses on them?
MAGNIFYING_MARGARET: “Reading glasses on my nose, distance glasses on my head. I can see everything except where I put either pair.”
FRAME_OF_MIND: “Those are two PAIRS of glasses, Margaret.”
MAGNIFYING_MARGARET: “Thank you. I now have twice as many missing.”
MODERATOR: “For drinking glasses, please use the homeware section. This is the third time this week.”
